description: Evolutionary framework for recursive self-improvement under non-stationary utilities by organizing search into epochs with controlled utility evolution; incorporates agent-as-a-judge signals.
training_prompt: Design an RSI loop with epoch-based objectives: propose (1) an agent improvement operator, (2) an evaluator update operator, and (3) a safety constraint that must remain invariant across epochs. Then simulate one epoch transition using a toy task.
expected_improvement: recursive_self_improvement_rate via non-stationary evaluator co-evolution; metacognition_accuracy via explicit judge panels.

description: Jointly updates a long-term natural-language experiential rule pool and agent policy from the same trajectories; retrieves task-relevant rules at decision time and revises the rule pool post-episode.
training_prompt: Given a sequence of 5 interaction episodes with successes/failures, extract experiential rules, propose how to revise them using comparisons to successful trajectories, and show how the next action is conditioned on retrieved rules + history.
expected_improvement: skill_acquisition_rate and transfer_learning_rate by aligning externalized rules with evolving policy; sample_efficiency_trend by reusing trajectories for both rules and policy updates.

technique: Semantic early stopping for agent loops
description: Stops iterative LLM agent loops when consecutive drafts stop changing semantically (embedding distance + patience), reducing unnecessary iterations and token spend.
training_prompt: You are running a Writer/Critic loop. Propose a semantic early-stopping rule using embedding similarity and a patience window. Given 6 draft summaries, decide at which iteration to stop and justify with a computed similarity table.
expected_improvement: sample_efficiency_trend by reducing wasted tokens in multi-step agent loops; agentic_capability_score by preventing truncation on hard cases via adaptive iteration budgets.

description: Contrastive regularizer that encourages actions to depend on task instructions, mitigating task-insensitive shortcut behavior and improving OOD generalization for language agents.
training_prompt: Create a pair of similar tasks with subtly different goals. Show how an agent's action distribution should change when the task instruction is perturbed. Propose a contrastive loss term that penalizes identical actions under instruction perturbations.
expected_improvement: transfer_learning_rate and zero_shot_success_count by improving sensitivity to task instructions under distribution shift; metacognition_accuracy via attention stability to task tokens.

description: Decomposes evaluation criteria into atomic binary questions answered independently, producing interpretable multi-dimensional scores and question-level feedback usable for prompt self-improvement.
training_prompt: Given an LLM output and an evaluation rubric, generate 10 atomic yes/no evaluation questions, answer them, and aggregate into a multi-dimensional score. Then propose a prompt revision guided by the failed questions.
expected_improvement: metacognition_accuracy via interpretable self-evaluation; skill_acquisition_rate via faster prompt iteration using question-level feedback.

technique: RiVER (RL without ground-truth via ranking-calibrated continuous rewards)
description: Trains LLMs on score-based optimization tasks without ground-truth solutions by calibrating continuous execution rewards to avoid scale/frequency dominance, improving transfer to exact-solution coding benchmarks.
training_prompt: Design an RL training loop for score-based coding tasks where only an execution score is available. Specify a reward calibration method using instance-wise comparisons and top-rank emphasis, and explain how it avoids scale dominance and frequency dominance.
expected_improvement: agentic_capability_score and sample_efficiency_trend by expanding verifiable-RL to non-ground-truth tasks; zero_shot_success_count via transfer to exact-solution benchmarks.

technique: GeoAlign (directional-consensus rollout curation for LLM RL)
description: Stabilizes online LLM reinforcement learning under noisy rewards by detecting directionally inconsistent rollouts in representation space and replacing them with within-prompt stable alternatives.
training_prompt: You have 8 rollouts for the same prompt with reward scores and hidden-state vectors. Compute reward-ordered displacement directions, find the consensus prototype direction, flag outliers by angular deviation, and show how curated rollouts change the policy update.
expected_improvement: sample_efficiency_trend and recursive_self_improvement_rate by reducing oscillation/variance in RL updates; metacognition_accuracy by surfacing inconsistency signals.

technique: Agent memory layer (lightweight memory for agents)
description: Lightweight memory layer for agents; relevant as an implementation reference for persistent knowledge/memory in agent systems.
training_prompt: Draft a minimal memory API (store/retrieve/summarize/evict) for DMAI agents. Then write a scenario where the agent must use stored memories to improve performance on a repeated task without leaking irrelevant context.
expected_improvement: agentic_capability_score and transfer_learning_rate by improving long-horizon memory use; multi_modal_integration_score if extended to store multimodal embeddings.

description: Framework for programmatically optimizing and compiling LM pipelines; useful for turning prompt-tuned components into optimized modules with measurable improvements.
training_prompt: Convert a DMAI prompt-based skill into a modular pipeline with explicit input/output signatures. Define an optimization objective (e.g., factuality or success rate) and describe how you would compile/optimize the module using automated evaluation.
expected_improvement: skill_acquisition_rate via systematic optimization loops; metacognition_accuracy via explicit metrics-driven compilation rather than ad-hoc prompting.
